analysis-data.cards.sentimento.text3: In the market, Lula fell 1.00pp to 62.50% (vol USD 7.73M), and the level caveat matters: this is not a drop in level, it is the same value as Jul 25 and Jul 27, with the top of the AFOS series having marked 63.50% on Jul 26 and Jul 28. Flávio rose 0.10pp to 23.95% (vol USD 7.70M), and the daily close of the series records his FOURTH consecutive advance, up from 22.90% on Jul 25. Renan Santos fell 0.05pp to 8.70% (vol USD 8.59M), but the number of his that matters today is another one: with 7.8% in the polling, the distance between price and declared vote fell to 0.90pp, and in this round it narrowed on the POLLING side, which rose, and not on the price side, as had been happening since June. Caiado inverted the signal of the two previous sessions: he rose 0.45pp in the winner contract, to 2.35%, and fell 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 25.50%, with Renan recovering 1.00pp in that book, to 61.50%. Zema rose 0.20pp, to 0.75%. Total accumulated volume in the presidential book at USD 116.49M. Capture note: the double-reading guard ran THREE times today. It rejected the first round over a 1.00pp divergence in Renan Santos's third place, approved the second with no divergence at all, and on the third, run at 19:50 to check the market before the editorial close, it rejected again, this time ONLY on Michelle Bolsonaro's book, which swung between 0.35% and 0.55%. Every other price repeated and enters FIRM; Michelle's enters as a declared RANGE.
analysis-data.cards.sentimento.direita: Flávio rose 0.10pp to 23.95% (vol USD 7.70M), a fourth consecutive daily close on the rise in the AFOS series, up from 22.90% on Jul 25. In the sub-markets, he ROSE 0.50pp in first-round second place, to 78.50%, and FELL 1.50pp in third place, to 6.25%. In the polling, [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) has him at 35.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), a 0.8pp retreat against the institute's Jul 1 round, and at 42.9% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The hardest number for him is the 52.9% rejection, the highest among those tested, which sits 17.1pp above his own voting intention; for Lula that distance is 4.5pp. Among state polls, the day was good where the votes are: he leads São Paulo in BOTH rounds, 34% x 30% in the first and 40% x 35% in the runoff (Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest), n=1,650, field Jul 23 to 27, BR-09998/2026). On the institutional front, the bill for his own convention arrived: Jair Bolsonaro's defence told the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) he did NOT authorise the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video, after Moraes gave 48 hours on Jul 28, while Flávio's campaign told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão, Jul 29). He still has no running mate, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away.
analysis-data.cards.sentimento.terceiraVia: The pack inverted the signal of the two previous days, and the inversion is in Caiado. He had been rising in the third-place book and falling in the winner book; today he RISES 0.45pp in the winner, to 2.35% (vol USD 5.20M), and FALLS 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 25.50%. The 2.35% of this capture sits above every daily close of the AFOS series since Jun 20, when the series marked 2.30%, and the series maximum is 2.40%, from Apr 14 and Jun 19. Except that the polling went hard against him: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) has him at 3.1% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), half the 6% from [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) two days earlier, and in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) it has him losing 48.2% to 38.9%, far from the [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) of 45% to 43% in that survey. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 gained a third measurement and it landed on [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha)'s side. Politically it was his best day: Tarcísio de Freitas freed allies and base mayors, on Jul 28, to back his candidacy (CNN Brasil) and he began attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure (Folha de S.Paulo). The pack's best polling number, though, belongs to Haddad, for a reason of method: it is NATIONAL. In one of AtlasIntel's scenarios without Lula he ties statistically with Flávio, 44.3% to 43.7%, and his price in the first-round second-place book rose 0.30pp, to 1.15%, while the winner contract stayed at 0.25%. Zema rose 0.20pp to 0.75%, and the national poll reframes yesterday's state number: in the national runoff he loses 48.6% to 39.6%. Michelle had no price confirmed by the guard and enters as a RANGE of 0.35% to 0.55%, Jair stayed at 1.05%, Alckmin rose 0.10pp to 0.35% and Camilo Santana fell 0.05pp to 0.35%.

Senate by seats: [PL](/en/glossary#pl) 71.00% (flat) and [MDB](/en/glossary#mdb) 17.60% (up 0.35pp). Impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice at 3.35% (UP 0.55pp). Total accumulated volume in the presidential book at USD 116.49M. Capture Jul 29, 22:50 UTC, on the guard's third round, which confirmed every book except Michelle's.
analysis-data.cards.inss.text3: The market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice ROSE 0.55pp to 3.35% (vol USD 83,000), and here the record that matters is the DIRECTION, not the size: the price moved up on the week's densest day in institutional facts, after falling 0.60pp the day before. The day carried Jair Bolsonaro's defence told Moraes he did not authorise the artificial-intelligence video shown at the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) justices began seeing abuse in the use of AI in campaigning, and the STF is preparing to act should the TSE not punish. The method caveat is worth more than the number: with USD 83,000 in accumulated volume against USD 116.49M in the presidential book, this market moves on very little money, and 0.55pp in it is very little money. What real money did was move in the direction of the pile-up, in a contract too small to turn that into priced removal risk.
analysis-data.cards.inss.text4: On inflation, the shift the panel recorded yesterday undid itself in a single session, and that is the day's lesson about small books. The modal band went BACK to 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, while the 4.50% to 4.99% band fell from 39.25% to 34.90% and the 5.50% to 5.99% band collapsed from 12.20% to 4.10%. In other words, the centre of the distribution climbed back the step it had come down yesterday. The two caveats still matter more than the numbers: the whole book adds up to USD 81,000, and the inflation market is NOT covered by the double-reading guard, which watches only the five electoral books. Changing modal band two days in a row in a book that size is noise, and the honest record is that yesterday's reading did not hold.
analysis-data.cards.inss.impactoGestao: Fresh reading on government performance: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29 brings 37.9% great or good, 12.7% fair and 49.3% bad or terrible. [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27 measured 36% x 20% x 43%, and [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) of Jul 24 measured 32% x 28% x 38%. The three institutes disagree on the level and agree on the sign: the administration is rated worse than the person, and the distance between the two indicators persists. In AtlasIntel that distance is 9.7pp, with 47.6% approving his performance and 37.9% calling the administration great or good. On inflation, the modal band went back to 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, ahead of the 4.50% to 4.99% band, which fell to 34.90%, in a book that adds up to USD 81,000 and does not pass through the capture guard.
analysis-data.cards.inss.conclusao: With 67 days to the election, Wednesday inverted Tuesday. Yesterday there was no national polling and the favourite's price rose 1.00pp; today the largest-sample poll of the window came out and the price fell 1.00pp, to 62.50%, returning the point taken the day before. The polling says stability: against the same institute's Jul 1 round, BOTH front-runners fall and the gap narrows 0.6pp, all inside the 1pp margin. Two findings remain from the day. The first is about Renan Santos: with 7.8% in the polling and 8.70% in price, the distance fell to 0.90pp, and in this round it narrowed on the POLLING side, which rose, and not on the price side, as had been happening since June. The second is about Caiado: the winner price rose 0.45pp on the same day the polling cut him in half, from 6% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) to 3.1%, and the third measurement on him landed on [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha)'s side. On the institutional axis, the week's densest day was the only one where real money followed the direction: impeachment of an STF justice rose 0.55pp, to 3.35%, in a book of USD 83,000, where that is very little money. And the state polls completed the picture of a split country by adding the largest electoral college: Flávio leads São Paulo in both rounds, Lula dominates the Northeast with 52% in Bahia and 54% in Ceará, and Minas Gerais remains a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico).
analysis-data.cards.bancoMaster.text1: Wednesday brought a promotion in status, not a fresh fact, and the difference matters to this panel's method. What the previous day recorded as an exclusive report by Valor Econômico, namely that André Mendonça authorised the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) to trace assets abroad belonging to Daniel Vorcaro and others involved, appeared on Wednesday across several newsrooms (Gazeta do Povo, Imirante, Diario de Pernambuco, Tribuna da Internet), so the reporting is no longer single-sourced. The correction is the date: the decision was SIGNED IN MAY and only became public on Jul 28. The route is international cooperation under a mutual legal assistance treaty, run by the Justice Ministry's asset recovery department, and among the targets cited is a yacht valued at R$ 500 million. Yesterday the panel treated the act as if it were from the previous day; today the correct date goes on the record.
analysis-data.cards.bancoMaster.text3: On price, the record is the usual one and it is worth repeating with the exact number: the market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice rose 0.55pp to 3.35%, in a book of USD 83,000. On a volume that size, 0.55pp costs very little money, and the panel attributes the move to NOTHING in particular. Wednesday carried the fallout of the artificial-intelligence video at the STF, the government's reading of the extension of the US emergency, Dino's decision on parliamentary amendments and three state polls. Choosing which of those events moved 0.55pp in a book of USD 83,000 would be inventing precision the data does not have.
analysis-data.cards.bancoMaster.conclusao: The three fronts of the Master case remain on separate tracks and should not be added together: the criminal one, at the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) under Mendonça as rapporteur, now with asset tracing abroad confirmed by several newsrooms, in a decision signed in May and revealed on Jul 28; the property one, in the Rio courts, with a freeze of up to R$ 135 million already set; and the legislative one, dammed up for four months in a writ of mandamus that is not being judged. Wednesday's news is about the quality of the information, not about progress: the item that entered yesterday from a single source now has a second newsroom behind it. When the path of parliamentary investigation stalls in a decision that never comes, the cost does not show up in market price, it shows up in time, and today's 3.35%, in a book of USD 83,000, measures how little real money prices that axis.
analysis-data.cards.stf.moraes: The day's most active front, and it was born inside the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention. After giving 48 hours on Jul 28 for Jair Bolsonaro's defence to explain the artificial-intelligence video carrying the former president's image and voice, citing risk of a fresh breach of his precautionary measures, he received the answer on Wednesday: the defence stated that Bolsonaro did NOT authorise the use of his own image and voice, and argued that he could not have done so because his visits are suspended for thirty days and Flávio is barred from visiting him for ninety, adding that he DOES NOT OBJECT to relatives producing this kind of content, a practice the filing calls notorious and continuous (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão, G1, Jul 29). The same day, Flávio's campaign told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters, and the [PT](/en/glossary#pt) petitioned the TSE over another AI piece, in which Flávio flies a fighter jet alongside Javier Milei. The panel records the positions and projects no outcome.
analysis-data.cards.stf.mendonca: He remains rapporteur of the inquiry opened on Jul 23 into Vorcaro's transfers for the film about Jair Bolsonaro, and the authorisation for the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) to trace assets abroad belonging to the former banker and others involved, published as an exclusive by Valor Econômico on Jul 28, appeared on Wednesday across several newsrooms, and the decision itself is from MAY, made public only on Jul 28, under a mutual legal assistance treaty run by the Justice Ministry's asset recovery department.
analysis-data.cards.stf.analise: The market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice before 2027 ROSE 0.55pp to 3.35% (vol USD 83,000). The method caveat comes before the reading, and in this case it is practically the whole reading: 0.55pp in a book of USD 83,000, against USD 116.49M in the presidential book, is very little money, and does not license talk of repriced risk. With that said, the record that matters is the contrast. This was the week's densest day in institutional facts: the former president's defence told the STF he did not authorise the artificial-intelligence video shown at his own son's convention, and Moraes had already said that, in that scenario, the piece may amount to a deep fake barred by electoral law, with liability for Flávio and the party; [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) justices came to see abuse and want to curb AI in campaigning; the STF is preparing to act should the TSE not punish; Dino set a deadline for Congress on the amendments axis; and the President of the Republic publicly complained about corporatism among judges and prosecutors. And here the pattern this panel has recorded since June bends a little: faced with that pile-up, real money DID move, and upward. It is the same pattern this panel has recorded since June: the market treats institutional friction as friction, and not as probability of a justice being removed.

analysis-criteriosa.subtitle: UPDATE Jul 29, 19:50 BRT, with 67 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). THE DAY IS THE EXACT INVERSE OF THE ONE BEFORE: yesterday there was no national polling and the favourite's price rose 1.00pp; today the national poll with the largest sample in the window came out and the favourite's price FELL 1.00pp, to 62.50%, with the gap over Flávio easing from +39.65pp to +38.55pp. THE POLLING: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg (n=5,021, field Jul 22 to 27, 1pp margin, BR-08602/2026, cost of R$ 80,000, self-funded) has Lula 44.9% x Flávio 35.8% in the first round, a gap of 9.1pp, with Renan Santos 7.8%, Caiado 3.1% and Zema 2.8%. Lula wins the SIX [runoffs](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) he appears in, and the tightest margin is 5.3pp against JAIR Bolsonaro (49.2% to 43.9%), not against Flávio, who sits at 6.3pp. In the two scenarios without Lula, Haddad 44.3% x Flávio 43.7%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico), and Alckmin 45.8% x Flávio 42.7%. Approval of Lula 47.6% against 51.2% disapproval. Rejection: Flávio 52.9%, Lula 49.4% and Jair 42.6%. Against the institute's own Jul 1 round, BOTH front-runners fall and the first-round gap narrows from 9.7pp to 9.1pp, all inside the 1pp margin, so the honest reading of the polling is stability. THE DIRECTION MATCHES, THE SIZE DOES NOT: the poll narrowed the gap by 0.6pp and the market narrowed by 1.10pp in the same session, and the panel records the coincidence without claiming cause. THE METHOD FINDING is in Renan Santos: 7.8% in the polling against 8.70% in price leaves the distance at 0.90pp, and in this round it narrowed on the POLLING side, which rose, and not on the price side, as had been happening. CAIADO INVERTED yesterday's signal: he rose 0.45pp in the winner book, to 2.35%, and fell 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 25.50%, on the same day the polling cut him in half, from 6% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) to 3.1%. THE INSTITUTIONAL AXIS was born inside the [PL](/en/glossary#pl)'s own convention: after Moraes gave 48 hours on Jul 28, Jair Bolsonaro's defence answered on Wednesday that he did NOT authorise the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video, while Flávio told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters. And the one market that did follow that pile-up was impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice, which ROSE 0.55pp, to 3.35%, in a book of USD 83,000, where 0.55pp is very little money. Total accumulated volume in the presidential book at USD 116.49M. Cross-reading with live [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) Jul 29, 22:50 UTC: the double-reading guard ran THREE times today. It rejected the first round over a 1.00pp divergence in Renan Santos's third place, approved the second, and on the third, at 19:50, rejected again, this time ONLY on Michelle Bolsonaro's book, which swung between 0.35% and 0.55%. Every other price enters firm; Michelle's enters as a RANGE.

analysis-criteriosa.candidates[1].fracos[3]: Jair Bolsonaro's defence told the STF that he did NOT authorise the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video shown at the PL convention, and Moraes had already said that, in that scenario, the piece may amount to a deep fake barred by electoral law, with liability for him and the party.
analysis-criteriosa.candidates[1].analise: His day has two layers moving in opposite directions, and the panel needs to keep them apart. On price, it was another day of small, persistent gains: he rose 0.10pp, to 23.95% (vol USD 7.70M), and the daily close of the AFOS series records a fourth consecutive advance, moving from 22.90% on Jul 25 to 24.00% today. Because the favourite fell 1.00pp, the gap against him narrowed 1.10pp and went to +38.55pp, the narrowest since Jul 24 by the daily close. In the sub-markets the picture is one of a settled position: he ROSE 0.50pp in first-round second place, to 78.50%, and FELL 1.50pp in third place, to 6.25%. A name rising in the second-place contract and falling in the third-place one is a name the market has already decided where to put. In the polling, the layer is different. [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29 has him at 35.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), a 0.8pp retreat against the institute's Jul 1 round, and at 42.9% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) against 49.2% for Lula. The number that weighs most is none of those: it is the 52.9% rejection, the highest among those tested, which sits 17.1pp above his own voting intention. For Lula, the same distance is 4.5pp. That describes a candidacy with a ceiling, not with a trajectory, and it is a structural constraint, not a fact of the day. There is also the finding internal to the survey: JAIR Bolsonaro loses the runoff by 5.3pp and he loses by 6.3pp, with the 1.0pp difference at the edge of the margin. By the same institute and in the same field period, the father's name does not test worse than the son's. Among the state polls, the day was good where the votes are: he leads São Paulo in both rounds, 34% to 30% in the first and 40% to 35% in the runoff. And it was bad in the Northeast, with 18% in Bahia and 23% in Ceará. On the institutional front, Wednesday collected the bill for his own convention: after Moraes gave 48 hours on Jul 28, Jair Bolsonaro's defence answered on Wednesday that he did NOT authorise the use of his image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão, Jul 29), while his campaign told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters (Folha de S.Paulo). The panel records both positions and projects no outcome.

analysis-criteriosa.candidates[2].analise: His day is the most interesting in the panel in terms of method, and the number that matters is not the price. On price, he fell 0.05pp to 8.70% (vol USD 8.59M), with a 0.45pp fall in first-round second place, to 11.70%, and a 1.00pp recovery in third place, to 61.50%. In other words, of the three books he appears in, two gave way and one returned part of what it had lost to Caiado. What actually changes is the distance this panel has tracked since June. [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, with n=5,021 and a 1pp margin, has him at 7.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). Against 8.70% in price, the distance between implied probability and declared voting intention sits at 0.90pp. And the point worth recording is the MECHANICS, not the size: in previous weeks that distance narrowed because the price gave way, while the polling stayed at 3%; in this round it narrowed because the POLLING rose, and rose in the largest-sample poll of the window. Those are two different things happening to the same number, and the second is more relevant than the first, because it means the declared vote moved in the direction the price was already pointing. The usual caveat still holds: probability of victory and voting intention are different quantities and cannot be subtracted from one another as if they measured the same thing, and the panel records the proximity as a distance between quantities, not as anyone being right. The dispersion between institutes, on the other hand, did not resolve: 9% at Real Time on Jul 21, 7.8% at AtlasIntel today, 6% at PoderData/Aya on Jul 16, 5% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Jul 27 and 3% at [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), Gerp and Indexa all still stand. Six percentage points of spread between institutes for the same name in the same month is the data point this panel cannot reduce. In the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), AtlasIntel gives Lula's most comfortable scenario in the whole survey against him: 47.6% to 30.2%, 17.4pp of distance. Series caveat: 8.70% is neither a maximum nor a minimum, with a peak of 17.90% on Jun 9 and a floor of 5.30% on Apr 26. And a capture note that concerns him in particular: his third place was the ONLY book the guard rejected in the first round, with a 1.00pp divergence between the two readings, and the 61.50% published is the value that repeated in the three following readings.

analysis-criteriosa.candidates[3].analise: The pack inverted the signal of the two previous sessions, and the inversion matters more than the size of the numbers. Caiado had been rising sharply in the third-place book and falling in the winner book; today he did exactly the opposite, RISING 0.45pp in the winner, to 2.35%, and FALLING 1.00pp in third place, to 25.50%. On the other side of that ledger is Renan Santos, who recovered 1.00pp in that same book. The detail that gives the move meaning is the polling, and it went against Caiado: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, with n=5,021 and a 1pp margin, has him at 3.1% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), half the 6% from [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) two days earlier, and in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) it has him losing 48.2% to 38.9%. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 between Nexus (45% to 43%) and [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) (47% to 40%) gained the third measurement it was missing, and it landed on Datafolha's side. In other words, the winner price rose on the day the polling got worse, and the panel records the divergence of direction without picking which of the two is right. Politically it was his best day: Tarcísio de Freitas freed allies and base mayors, on Jul 28, to back his candidacy and he began attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure. The pack's best polling number, though, belongs neither to him nor to Zema, but to Haddad, for a reason of method: it is NATIONAL. In one of AtlasIntel's two scenarios without Lula, Haddad ties statistically with Flávio, 44.3% to 43.7%, the tightest result of the whole round, and his price in the first-round second-place book rose 0.30pp, to 1.15%, while the winner contract stayed flat at 0.25%. The caveat is that this scenario is a polling hypothesis and not a candidacy under way. Zema rose 0.20pp, to 0.75%, and today's national poll reframes yesterday's state number: in the national runoff he loses 48.6% to 39.6%. Michelle had no price confirmed by the guard and enters as a RANGE of 0.35% to 0.55%, Jair stayed at 1.05%, Alckmin rose 0.10pp to 0.35% and Camilo Santana fell 0.05pp to 0.35%. The usual method caveat: these are prices between 0.15% and 2.35% in a book where the favourite is worth 62.50%, so a change in percentage points looks large in relative terms and is small in money.

analysis-criteriosa.cruzamento: Jul 29 was the exact inverse of the day before, and the inversion is the finding itself. Yesterday there was NO national polling and the favourite's price ROSE 1.00pp. On Wednesday the national poll with the largest sample in the window came out and the favourite's price FELL 1.00pp, from 63.50% to 62.50% (vol USD 7.73M), with the gap over Flávio easing from +39.65pp to +38.55pp. Before any reading, the level caveat, because it avoids a mistake this panel has already made: 62.50% is not a drop in level, it is the same level as Jul 25 and Jul 27, and the top of the AFOS series marked 63.50% on Jul 26 and Jul 28. By the daily close of the series, today's gap is the narrowest since Jul 24. THE POLLING OF THE DAY is [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg (field Jul 22 to 27, n=5,021, 1pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-08602/2026, cost of R$ 80,000, self-funded), and it is the largest sample in the window, ahead of the 5,000 of the institute's own Jul 1 round, with the smallest margin, tied at 1pp with that same round. In the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Lula 44.9%, Flávio Bolsonaro 35.8%, Renan Santos 7.8%, Ronaldo Caiado 3.1%, Romeu Zema 2.8%, Samara Martins 2.1% and Augusto Cury 1.6%. In a scenario reduced to five names, Lula goes to 47.4% and Flávio to 37.0%. In the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), Lula wins the SIX scenarios he appears in, and here is the data point the panel is obliged to highlight: his tightest margin is NOT against Flávio, it is against JAIR Bolsonaro, 49.2% to 43.9%, a difference of 5.3pp against the 6.3pp of the scenario with the son. The distance between the two scenarios, 1.0pp, sits at the edge of the margin, so this undoes no tie and instead suggests that, by the same institute and in the same field period, the father's name tests equal to or better than the son's. In the two scenarios WITHOUT Lula, Haddad 44.3% x Flávio 43.7%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) inside the margin, and Alckmin 45.8% x Flávio 42.7%. Rejection is the round's hardest number: Flávio 52.9%, Lula 49.4% and Jair 42.6%. And the comparison that matters more than the contest between institutes: Flávio's rejection sits 17.1pp above his own first-round voting intention, 35.8%, while for Lula that distance is 4.5pp, 49.4% against 44.9%. That is a structural constraint, not a data point of the day. Against the same institute's Jul 1 round, BOTH front-runners fall, Lula from 46.3% to 44.9% and Flávio from 36.6% to 35.8%, and the first-round gap narrows from 9.7pp to 9.1pp. In the direct runoff, the gap moves from 6.5pp to 6.3pp. With a 1pp margin, each of those moves fits in the noise, and the honest reading of the polling is STABILITY, not advance or retreat. What moves outside the margin is the government rating: Lula's approval rises 1.7pp, from 45.9% to 47.6%, and disapproval falls 1.1pp, from 52.3% to 51.2%, keeping disapproval ahead by the same method. ON THE COINCIDENCE between the fall in price and the narrowing in the poll, the panel records the direction and does NOT claim cause, for two reasons. First, the sizes differ: the poll narrowed the gap by 0.6pp and the market narrowed by 1.10pp. Second, the same session carried two other events capable of moving price, and the panel has no instrument to separate the contributions. Picking a cause here would be inventing precision the data does not have. THE METHOD FINDING OF THE DAY is in Renan Santos, and it is about the mechanics of convergence, not the level. With 7.8% in the polling and 8.70% in price, the distance between implied probability and declared voting intention fell to 0.90pp. In previous weeks that distance narrowed because the PRICE gave way, while the polling stayed at 3%; in this round it narrowed because the POLLING rose, and rose in the largest-sample poll of the window. Those are two different things happening to the same number, and the second is more relevant, because it means the declared vote moved in the direction the price was already pointing. It still holds that probability of victory and voting intention are different quantities, that they do not subtract from one another as if they measured the same thing, and that convergence is proof of no one being right. The dispersion between institutes, incidentally, did not resolve with the largest sample in the window: 9% at Real Time on Jul 21, 7.8% at AtlasIntel today, 6% at PoderData/Aya on Jul 16, 5% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Jul 27 and 3% at [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), Gerp and Indexa all still stand. Six percentage points of spread between institutes for the same name in the same month is the data point this panel cannot reduce, and it is more informative than any average. THE THIRD AXIS is Caiado, and he inverted the signal of the two previous sessions. He had been rising sharply in the third-place book and falling in the winner book; today he RISES 0.45pp in the winner, to 2.35%, and FALLS 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 25.50%, with Renan Santos recovering 1.00pp in that same book. The 2.35% of this capture sits above every daily close of the AFOS series since Jun 20, when the series marked 2.30%, and the series maximum is 2.40%. Except that the polling of the day went against him, and hard: 3.1% in the first round, half the 6% BTG/Nexus measured two days earlier, and a runoff of 48.2% to 38.9%, a distance of 9.3pp, far from the statistical tie of 45% to 43% in that survey and closer to the 47% to 40% of Datafolha on Jul 24. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 between Nexus and Datafolha gained the third measurement it was missing and it landed on Datafolha's side. Price rising and polling worsening on the same day is a divergence of direction, and the panel records both without choosing which is right. Politically, though, it was his best day: Tarcísio de Freitas freed allies and base mayors, on Jul 28, to back his presidential candidacy (CNN Brasil) and he adopted the strategy of attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure, saying that Flávio lost his own convention to an Argentine and an avatar (Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, Pleno.News). THE FOURTH AXIS is institutional, it is the strongest of the week, and it was born inside the [PL](/en/glossary#pl)'s own convention. On the night of Jul 28, Moraes gave 48 hours for Jair Bolsonaro's defence to say whether he authorised the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video shown at Flávio's convention, citing risk of a fresh breach of his precautionary measures (O Globo, G1, Estadão). On Wednesday the defence answered that he did NOT authorise it (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão), while Flávio's campaign told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters (Folha de S.Paulo). The [PT](/en/glossary#pt) petitioned the TSE over another AI video, in which Flávio flies a fighter jet alongside Javier Milei. TSE justices see abuse and want to curb the excessive use of AI in campaigns, and the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) is preparing to act should the TSE not punish (Estadão, O Globo). The same day, Lula publicly complained about corporatism among judges and prosecutors and argued for institutional reform (Folha de S.Paulo), and Dino ordered the government and Congress to specify the responsibility of members of parliament over amendments, with a 10-day deadline (G1, Folha de S.Paulo). And the one market that followed that pile-up was impeachment of an STF justice, which ROSE 0.55pp to 3.35%, in a book of USD 83,000, after falling 0.60pp the day before. Recording the direction is mandatory; building a narrative on it is not, because 0.55pp on USD 83,000 is very little money. In the Master case, the record is one of method and it is a promotion in status: what the previous day carried as an exclusive report by Valor Econômico, namely that André Mendonça authorised the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) to trace assets abroad belonging to Daniel Vorcaro, appeared on Wednesday across several newsrooms, and with a date correction that matters: the decision was signed in MAY and only became public on Jul 28. THE FIFTH AXIS is external. Trump extended the national emergency over Brazil for a year on Jul 28, and on Wednesday the matter changed in nature: the Brazilian government came to read the extension as possible preparation for new sanctions (O Globo, Valor Econômico), and the PL campaign leadership expects US measures against Alexandre de Moraes (O Globo). In parallel, US senators accused the Trump administration of promoting conspiracy theories about the Brazilian elections (G1, CBN). THE SIXTH AXIS is inflation, and it carries a lesson about small books worth more than the number. The modal band went BACK to 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, while the 4.50% to 4.99% band fell from 39.25% to 34.90% and the 5.50% to 5.99% band collapsed from 12.20% to 4.10%. In other words, the shift the panel recorded yesterday undid itself in a single session. In a book that adds up to USD 81,000 and is NOT covered by the double-reading guard, changing modal band two days in a row is noise, and the honest record is that yesterday's reading did not hold. THE STATE POLLS OF THE DAY do not enter the panel's national window, by scope rule, but their content completes the picture of a split country and now includes the largest electoral college. Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) in São Paulo (n=1,650, field Jul 23 to 27, 2pp margin, BR-09998/2026 and SP-04846/2026) has Flávio 34% x Lula 30% in the first round and Flávio 40% x Lula 35% in the runoff, plus Tarcísio 41% x Haddad 26% in the state race. Genial/Quaest in Bahia has Lula 52% x Flávio 18%, with ACM Neto and Jerônimo Rodrigues in a statistical tie in both rounds. Ipsos-Ipec in Ceará (n=800, field Jul 23 to 26, 3pp margin, BR-07235/2026) has Lula 54% x Flávio 23%. Adding what has already been published, Flávio wins São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, Lula wins the Northeast comfortably and Minas Gerais is a statistical tie. A CAPTURE NOTE, and it is about process. The double-reading guard ran THREE times today. It rejected the first round over a 1.00pp divergence in Renan Santos's third place, from 62.50% to 61.50%, approved the second with no divergence at all in the five electoral books, and on the third, run at 19:50 to check the market before the editorial close, rejected again, this time ONLY on Michelle Bolsonaro's book, which swung between 0.35% and 0.55%. The 61.50% published is the value that repeated in the readings after the first rejection. Every price enters FIRM, with one declared exception: Michelle's enters as a RANGE. Every price in this update enters firm and there is no range. Yesterday two rounds were blocked and the same kind of thin book showed up again today, which is consistent: first-round third place adds up to USD 484,000 against USD 116.49M in the presidential book, and a wide spread in a book that size is normal. Finally, the calendar: the week still brings PoderData on Jul 30 (n=2,400) and Vox Brasil on Jul 31 (n=2,100) to say whether the 62.50% level has polling behind it, and the Aug 5 deadline for naming running mates still applies to Flávio and to Zema.
